rationale:
Evidence: iteration 7 (kp 3.0, ki 1.0, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, outer sensors at x = ±0.04, sensor_size 0.016, last_direction) scored 216.97. Iteration 9 reproduced that exact design at 216.97 under the same seeds, so the result is confirmed. The ki series (0.8 → 184.93, 1.0 → 216.97, 1.2 → 187.18) peaks near 1.0. Earlier races rule out wider outer sensors (iteration 3), higher kp (iteration 4) and lower base_speed (iteration 2). Max_error stays near 0.06 m on every track, and the oval finish rate is only 0.2, so the open problems are the residual drift and the oval finish rate.

Change: base_speed 1.6 → 1.7, with every other field as in iteration 7. Iteration 2 showed that cutting speed to 1.2 removed oval finishes, so a modest rise is the more plausible direction. Oval mean finish time was 1.93 s at 1.6, which scales to about 1.82 s at 1.7 and stays well under the 3.0 s limit. Only one variable changes, so the race isolates speed.

Expected result: oval finish rate at or above 0.2 and a score at or above about 217. Hypothesis H7: the oval finishes are limited by time, and a small speed rise improves them without pushing the bends off track. Risk: higher speed may increase bend drift, so s-bend progress (0.462) and max_error are the watch items.

Fallback: if the score falls below 216.97, or s-bend or slalom progress drops with max_error above 0.063 m, return base_speed to 1.6 and submit the iteration 7 design unchanged. If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.35, that also favours the fallback.

Measurements wanted: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation, so the speed effect can be judged per track.
